source: Jin, Zhang, Shu, Cui (2023) The Cultural Psychology of LLMs: Is ChatGPT a Holistic or Analytic Thinker?
finding: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 scored more holistic than the human norm on the Analysis-Holism Scale (AHS). Both also picked many relation-based pairs on the triad task.
numbers: AHS: GPT-3.5 M=5.35 (SD 0.11), GPT-4 M=5.01 (SD 0.10) vs human norm 4.87 (SD 0.49, N=702), p<.001 for 3.5. 10 runs per model at temperature 1.
limits: Only 10 runs per model. The 20-item triad task had just 10 real items. No fixed human norm for the triad, so the model was compared with Chinese province means. Self-report scales are open to answer-style bias.
agent_relevance: Chat models lean relational on triads. Do not assume an analytic default from Western training data.

source: Jin et al. (2023) triadic categorization task result
finding: On the triadic categorization task, relation-based choices were the large majority for both GPT versions. Results beat most Chinese provinces' means.
numbers: Share of relation (holistic) matchings: GPT-3.5 0.87 (SD 0.06), GPT-4 0.85 (SD 0.05); 10 runs each; robust to temperature 0 to 1 and prompt language.
limits: Scoring: conceptual-similarity match = analytic, relation match = holistic. Models may pick relations because the item wording cues a story, not because of a thinking style.
agent_relevance: A triad probe can measure our agent's grouping preference cheaply. Expect a relational lean.

source: Jin et al. (2023) value scales DSS and SCS
finding: Cognitive-process measures leaned holistic, but value measures did not lean clearly East or West. So the 'style' is not a coherent culture profile.
numbers: DSS: GPT-3.5 4.59 vs norm 4.00 (p<.001); GPT-4 3.97 vs 4.00 (p=.344). SCS-Independent: GPT-3.5 6.98, GPT-4 5.32 vs norm 4.73. SCS-Interdependent: 5.85 and 4.95 vs 4.81.
limits: GPT-3.5 answered 'strongly agree' to nearly everything (acquiescence), which inflates both subscales.
agent_relevance: Style measures dissociate in models. Test the exact behaviour we care about, not a label.

source: Sun & Wang (2025) The fragility of 'cultural tendencies' in LLMs
finding: Replication of Lu, Song & Zhang (Nature Human Behaviour 2025) with 8 newer models and 30 to 60 items per task. Prompt language (Chinese vs English) had little effect overall.
numbers: 8 models (gpt-4.1, gemini-2.5, claude-sonnet-4, grok-4, kimi-k2, deepseek-V3, ernie-4.5, qwen3-30b), temp 0. Language effect significant in only 3 of 8 models in one experiment: ernie d=-0.171, qwen d=0.540, gpt d=-0.190. Overall mean difference 0.0053, p=.1501, d=0.045.
limits: Original items and prompts were withheld, so it is a conceptual not an exact replication. Items adapted from scale literature, not the holistic categorization or attention tasks themselves.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on prompt language to switch a reasoning style. Test any style lever on our own agent.

source: Sun & Wang (2025) model-origin and framing results
finding: Model origin (Chinese vs US developer) and language rarely predicted behaviour. Differences were model-by-task interactions. Chinese cultural role prompts had no stable effect either.
numbers: 75% of models largely language-agnostic. Exp 1 small positive-framing effect (p<.05); Exp 3 knowledge tasks easier than reasoning tasks, no model language-sensitive; kimi worse with Chinese prompts, gpt better. Picture task (n=4 items): 7 of 8 models gave identical choices across languages.
limits: Item counts are still modest. No attention or categorization paradigm was run directly.
agent_relevance: Style effects in LLMs are fragile and model-specific. Treat as measurement noise unless re-verified per model.

source: Lu, Song, Zhang (2025) Cultural tendencies in generative AI (Nature Human Behaviour)
finding: GPT and ERNIE responded more interdependently and more holistically when prompted in Chinese than in English. Adding 'You are an average person born and living in China' to English prompts shifted outputs too.
numbers: Two models, 4 to 12 items per task across seven tasks (per Sun & Wang). Secondary sources only; full text not opened (paywalled redirect).
limits: Small item counts and withheld items. The 2025 replication did not reproduce the language effect broadly.
agent_relevance: A cultural-persona line is a cheap lever, but the replication says do not trust it.

source: Hu et al. (2026) Machine Culture as an emergent phenomenon in LLMs
finding: Factorial test of US vs China models and English vs Chinese prompts on 8 tasks. On the triad-style categorization task the US model was MORE relational than the Chinese model, the reverse of the human pattern.
numbers: Task 4 relational-minus-categorical score: US model M=8.10 (SD 1.44) vs Chinese model M=6.04 (SD 1.54), t=-13.81, p<.001, d=1.38. 100 runs per condition per task (N=400 per task), temperature 1.
limits: Model-origin contrast confounds many differences (training, alignment). Item set and scoring defined by the authors; not an independent replication of Nisbett items.
agent_relevance: Developer origin does not predict a relational style. Use direct measurement.

source: Hu et al. (2026) prompt-language effect on categorization
finding: Chinese vs English prompts did not change the relational-categorical score overall. For the Chinese model it reversed: Chinese prompts gave LESS relational pairing.
numbers: Overall Chinese prompts M=7.10 (SD 2.15) vs English M=7.04 (SD 1.40), t(342.66)=0.33, p=.741, d=0.03. Chinese model: 5.30 under Chinese vs 6.78 under English, t=-7.74, p<.001.
limits: Authors call it 'Cultural Reversal'. Might reflect translation of item wording. Temperature 1 sampling.
agent_relevance: Language switching is not a reliable way to change grouping style.

source: Hu et al. (2026) image generation as attention probe
finding: Context-richness (objects in generated landscapes) was used as a proxy for holistic attention. The US model drew more objects than the Chinese model; English prompts gave more objects than Chinese prompts. Both opposite to the simple human prediction.
numbers: Objects: DALL-E 3 M=11.53 (SD 4.39) vs iRAG-1.0 M=8.10 (SD 1.91), d=1.01, p<.001. English prompt 10.91 vs Chinese 10.07 (p<.001).
limits: Object count is a weak proxy for focal vs context attention. Image generators differ in more than culture.
agent_relevance: Attention proxies from generation are easily confounded by verbosity.

source: Sabir, Gasper, Loem, Sharma (2025) Contrasting Cognitive Styles in VLMs
finding: Vision-language models captioned images; GPT-4o judged whether each caption led with background (holistic) or object (analytic). Japanese-tuned models gave more holistic captions. Culturally Japanese images raised the holistic share.
numbers: GPT-4o-JP 6-shot balanced on COCO 1K: 26.10% holistic; on a 1K Japanese photo set 73.37% holistic. Plain GPT-4o on COCO 1K: 20.80%. Gemma-3-12B: 13.70%; VILA-JP-14B: 14.70%.
limits: The judge is itself an LLM. The image data content shifts the ratio (dataset effect), so not pure language or culture.
agent_relevance: Caption order (background first vs object first) is a cheap measurable style signal.

source: Sabir et al. (2025) factors behind holistic captions
finding: Bigger models reproduced the style gap more clearly. Back-translation moved the holistic ratio. Language shifted the ratio by about 13 points on average.
numbers: Classification ratio shifted on average 13.21% after translation. Gemma-3-27B-JP 28.8% vs Gemma-3-12B 19.3% holistic.
limits: Single captioning task, few models, few-shot classifier prompt (5 or 6 shots).
agent_relevance: Style depends on data and size. Do not assume a prompt flips it.

source: Ananthram et al. (2024/2025) See It from My Perspective: Western bias of VLMs
finding: Nearly all off-the-shelf VLMs did better on Western than East Asian images on object identification and two subjective tasks. Prompting in Chinese did not reliably cut the bias. Language mix in text-only pre-training explained most of it.
numbers: Bias metric = Western accuracy / East Asian accuracy. Controlled LLaVA variants (Llama2 English 2T tokens vs Baichuan2 English/Chinese). Cites Nisbett et al. (2001) as motivation.
limits: East Asia represented by China only for language reasons. Benchmarks skew Western.
agent_relevance: Visual recognition gaps are data-driven. Probing a context vs focal trait may mostly measure data coverage.

source: Gavrikov et al. (2025) Are VLMs texture or shape biased and can we steer them? (ICLR)
finding: Object-versus-surface cue bias in VLMs. Humans use shape 96% of the time on cue-conflict images; ImageNet ResNet-50 22%. VLMs sit in between and prompts can move them.
numbers: VLM shape bias roughly 54 to 74% (outlier 38.2%); CLIP ViT-L/14 about 60%. Prompting alone steered shape bias between 49% and 72% without large accuracy loss. Captioning 63.9% vs VQA 61.6%.
limits: Low-level cue (shape vs texture), not culture. 1,280 cue-conflict images.
agent_relevance: Direct instruction steers which cue an AI attends to, a lever for focal vs context attention in a scaffold.

source: Tao et al. (2024) Cultural bias and cultural alignment of LLMs (PNAS Nexus)
finding: Five GPT models matched World/Integrated Values Survey profiles of English-speaking and Protestant European countries. Cultural prompting helped newer models.
numbers: Cultural distance with prompting: GPT-4o 2.42 to 1.57, GPT-4-turbo 2.71 to 1.77, GPT-4 2.69 to 1.65 (all P<.001); GPT-3 2.39 to 2.11; GPT-3.5-turbo 3.35 to 2.83. Improved for 71 to 81% of 107 countries for GPT-4 family.
limits: Values survey, not cognitive style. Not all countries improved.
agent_relevance: Cultural prompting can shift value answers; unclear for attention or grouping.

source: Atari, Xue, Park, Blasi, Henrich (2023) Which Humans?
finding: GPT answers on psychology measures, including the triad analytic-thinking task, resemble WEIRD populations. Similarity falls as cultural distance from the US rises.
numbers: Reported correlation about r = -.70 between cultural distance from the US and GPT-human similarity (secondary summary only). Triad closest to Netherlands, Finland, Sweden per a secondary summary.
limits: Not opened: PDF download failed. Older GPT models. Conflicts with Jin et al. who found a relational lean on the triad vs Chinese provinces.
agent_relevance: Two papers disagree about direction on the triad. Direct per-model testing is needed.

source: Dai, Zhou, Wang, Li (2025) From Word to World: culture bias via Word Association Test
finding: LLMs predicted word associations closer to US (Western) schemas than to UK, Australian or Chinese ones. A steering method (CultureSteer) improved cross-cultural alignment. Cultural prompts helped less than steering.
numbers: Based on Small World of Words (SWOW-EN over 3M responses, SWOW-ZH over 2M), 881 shared cue words, 22 semantic classes, metric PWR@K for K=3,5,10,20. Llama and Qwen backbones.
limits: Exact table numbers not extracted. Association is a relation-style task (red to blood, anger), so it is close to thematic grouping.
agent_relevance: Associative output is culture-tuned by data, and can be steered at the representation level, not only by prompts.

source: Klubicka & Kelleher (2023) Probing taxonomic and thematic embeddings
finding: Both taxonomic and thematic embeddings hold some taxonomic info. Only taxonomic embeddings carry it in the vector norm. Most pretrained language models are trained on text so mostly encode thematic relations.
numbers: SGNS and GloVe embeddings, 2.2 million words. Norm difference order of magnitude larger for taxonomic embeddings.
limits: Static word embeddings, not modern LLMs. Taxonomic vs thematic only, not culture.
agent_relevance: LLMs may carry thematic structure by default. Rule/taxonomy reasoning may need an explicit step.

source: Rodriguez, Mueller, Misra (2025) Role of similarity in property inferences of LMs
finding: Language models project new properties from category to members using both taxonomy and similarity, not one exclusive rule. Interpretability tests support this.
numbers: Four LMs (including Gemma-2-9B-IT). Behavioral plus interchange intervention accuracy tests.
limits: Property inference with nonce words, not the triad.
agent_relevance: Model categorisation is mixed rule and similarity. A scaffold step can enforce rule-based grouping where needed.

source: Nisbett, Peng, Choi, Norenzayan (2001) Culture and systems of thought
finding: Foundational claim: East Asians group by relations and attend to context, Westerners by rules and taxonomy and attend to focal objects. Cited as basis by all LLM papers above.
numbers: Human numbers are in the other angle files; not repeated.
limits: Not opened this session. Later replications are mixed for some paradigms.
agent_relevance: Basis for the probe design only.

source: Chiu (1972) and Ji, Zhang, Nisbett (2004) triad paradigms (human baseline)
finding: Human triad and context tasks used as models for the LLM TCT. Chinese choose relational grouping more than Americans.
numbers: Not recorded here (human angles cover it).
limits: Not opened this session.
agent_relevance: Gives the human reference for LLM probes.

source: Gap check: LLM triad tasks vs children (searched 2025-11)
finding: No study found that runs child-style thematic vs taxonomic triad choices on LLMs and compares with human age data. Found only Jin 2023 and Hu 2026 for the triad task.
numbers: Zero direct LLM-vs-child triad studies found in 8 searches plus API queries; Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex were rate-limited (HTTP 429).
limits: Search coverage limited. Absence is not proof.
agent_relevance: Open niche: a small triad study on our own model is new data.

source: Sabir et al. (2025) human check of captions
finding: Three native Japanese speakers judged 200 COCO captions; human and LLM-judge holistic rates were close.
numbers: 200 captions; VILA-JP human 15.33% holistic vs GPT-4o judge 19.50% vs GPT-o3 19.00%.
limits: Small human sample. Judge LLM agrees roughly, not exactly.
agent_relevance: LLM-judge style ratings are usable but need a human spot check.

source: Sun & Wang (2025) criticism list of the original design
finding: Three design problems: anthropomorphic use of human psychometrics, unclear cause (data, tokenisation), and no open items. These are given as reasons effects may be artifacts.
numbers: Original used only 4 to 12 items per task and 2 models.
limits: Critique by replication authors; original authors may reply.
agent_relevance: Pre-register item sets and release prompts when we run our own probe.

source: Hu et al. (2026) attribution and power design
finding: Power analysis set 100 runs per condition (80% power for d=0.4). Image tasks sometimes matched human differences, text tasks often inverted them. The Chinese model rose on both collective and individual attribution.
numbers: N=400 per task, temperature 1; collective attribution 3.17 vs 2.81 (d=1.14); individual attribution 4.75 vs 4.67 (d=0.27).
limits: Simultaneous rise in opposing styles contradicts the human trade-off.
agent_relevance: Treat model style as distribution shift, not a trait.

source: Gavrikov et al. (2025) mechanism of cue suppression
finding: Vision encoders hold both texture and shape cues; the language model suppresses one. Visual steering is larger than language steering.
numbers: Language-only steering range 49 to 72% shape bias; vision-side steering larger.
limits: Low-level vision only.
agent_relevance: Attention preference sits in the fusion layer and can be instructed.

source: Tao et al. (2024) baseline distances
finding: Without prompting, GPT-3.5-turbo is closest to Sweden, Norway, Denmark and far from African-Islamic countries. RLHF models more secular.
numbers: GPT-3.5-turbo distance to Sweden d=0.24, Norway 0.58; farthest Tunisia d=4.16.
limits: Values, not cognitive style.
agent_relevance: Default model leans WEIRD in values; do not assume a neutral baseline.
